recipes.name: Simple but Awesome Lemon Pepper Pork Chops

steps.text: Preheat oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
Tear off a generous square of tin foil for each chop, enough to wrap and seal completely. Coat both sides of each chop with lemon pepper.

Put 1 tablespoon butter and 1 tablespoon olive oil in the middle of each square of tin foil. Put the peppered chops on top of the butter and oil. Put 1 tablespoon of butter and 1 tablespoon olive oil on top of each chop. Add 1 teaspoon Worcestershire sauce over the top of each chop. Wrap each chop tightly and place on middle rack of oven. Bake for 35 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Simple but Awesome Lemon Pepper Pork Chops
raw_recipe.description: Melt-in-your-mouth pork chops coated with lemon pepper and baked in butter, olive oil and Worcestershire sauce.

review.reviewBody: I put olive oil in the bottom of a glass casserole dish just to coat, then arranged the chops in the dish. I dotted the chops with a little butter, added the seasonings (including a little garlic salt) and sealed the dish with foil before baking. Tender, easy, and good!

After reading the reviews of others, I decided to use this recipe as a guide and made a few changes. I used aluminum foil in a large casserole dish (this made clean up much easier). I brushed the olive oil on the aluminum foil and used boneless pork chops. I seasoned them with lemon pepper dry seasoning and steak and chop seasoning on both sides. I drizzled the Worcestershire sauce on each chop and then dropped a pad of butter and a clove of garlic on each of the pork chops. It took 45 minutes to cook these pork chops in this manner. They turned out juicy and tasty. I will use this method again.

My Family Loved this recipe. I took a few notes from other peoples reviews. I made sure I put the wrapped chops in a baking dish and glad I did because the juices really leaked! I also added a few garlic cloves and an extra tsp of Worcestershire sauce. And this was awesome! Really easy recipe with little prep, which is always a plus because I don't always have a lot of time. I definitely will be cooking this one again!

Nice, good pork recipe, very simple to follow as the name implies. Mine came out just a tad dry, but still flavorful. I would recommend, if you have extra time to prepare, marinating your chops. Definitely put the pork in a baking dish or sheet with a lip to catch the juices while in the oven. Maybe give them just 30 minutes or so to bake—that might rein in the dryness. I ended up spooning some of juices over because I did enjoy the lemon pepper taste.

I liked that this recipe was simple, I also customized it a little. I used regular black pepper, salt, & onion powder. I didn't have lemon pepper, and I didn't use Worcestershire sauce because that just sounded awful to me. I didn't have olive oil either. We had veggie oil and country crock butter at home. I didn't have foil either, and I only had two bone pork chops. It turned out juicy, and tender. It helps if you don't wrap it and can keep an eye on it, I started cooking at 400 but lowered it to 375 and it took 45 minutes to cook. Don't use too much oil & butter, I only used 1 tablespoon of oil and 1 of butter. You can add more as it cooks if you want. I basically had to substitute because I didn't have certain things, and because I didn't like the idea of using Worcestershire sauce. It turned out juicy, tender and best of all the recipe is simple enough you can make it your own. If you're looking for a simple pork chop dinner then this is. We had this with mashed potatoes and veggies. Even my bf liked it, I think it helps if you use bone pork chops. I really think that the bone makes a difference. I really loved the recipe didn't call for too many ingredients and that you can add or subtract to it and make it your own.

Made this tonight and it was a hit. I followed the advice of others before me: I marinated the chops in Worcestershire and EVOO for a few hours, and I added minced garlic on top of each chop. I also spread the butter (only about a total of 2 tsp per) on each side of the chops. I did not add any additional oil or Worcestershire sauce since they still had marinade on them. Then, to prevent the packs from leaking/getting holes in them (I used bone-in chops) I lined each piece of foil with a piece of parchment paper. The last change I made was to cook them on the grill. I used a med heat and put the chops on the top shelf. Delicious!

This is a wonderful recipe. Be sure to use bone-in pork chops. Also, I recommend pan searing until lightly golden brown before baking the pork chops. It seals in the juices. You don't need to bake them nearly as long as the recipe states. I would say 15-20 minutes at 400 is plenty. Absolutely place the foil wrapped chops in a dish or pan to avoid the juices running off and burning! Quite a bit of juice came out of the foil, but this was great as I was able to reserve the pan juices and pour them over the chops for extra flavor.
I'll definitely make it again. But next time, I will add some cumin to the dry rub and marinate overnight . And I would bake for 30 minutes instead. It was slightly dry.

This recipe is super easy to prepare, and that's why I loved it so much. I did exactly as the recipe stated, except I added some minced garlic on top of each pork chop. Also, the package of pork chops I had on hand were of different thickness/size, so I adjusted the butter/olive oil to each size. The pork chops were very tender. Next time I may add a little bit of chopped onion and mushroom with each pork chop to add a little bit of extra flavor. Also, yes, place the tin foil wrapped chops in a baking dish of some sort, because liquid will leak out. I will make again!

I didnt give it a 4 because it could be tweaked as follows: Rub lemon pepper (fresh is better!) on the chops. Sear pork chops with oil until golden brown on both sides. Place in buttered cassarole dish. top with pad of butter and worcestershire. top dish with a piece of foil. Bake in preheated oven until to desired doneness. The dish will turn out moist and delicious and not that icky white looking piece of meat in the picture.

First I made up a mixture of 1 tablespoon of lemon pepper seasoning, 1 tbsp of garlic powder, 1 tbsp onion powder, 1 tbsp of ground black pepper and mixed together. I got a bowl and poured in some olive oil and set aside and a stick of butter cut in 1 tbsp pats. I rinsed off my chops and let them dry. the mixture did about 6 chops before I had to mix another batch I had 19 chops to do. Process the next step one chop at a time so you don't hamper each chop being well seasoned.

Pinch up the seasoning mix and liberally hand sprinkle over both sides of the chop. Dip a basting brush in the olive oil and brush over both sides of your season chop. Put the chop in the center of foil paper top with a pat of butter and a tsp of Worchester sauce. Fold packet closed tightly. Do next chop the same way until you're finished.

I placed the foil packets in a bowl or pan overnight in the fridge. 

Take the packets out about 30 to 45 mins before cooking. Preheat oven to 400 and bake the packets for 35 to 45 min depending on your oven on a cookie sheet just in case packets leak. 

Take out and unwrap to let cool and serve. Put any leftover or make more to set on the table for those who want to add more to their chop.
Because I was worried about the tin foil leaking I baked the chops in PAM sprayed pie plates and covered with tin foil.

I followed this recipe exactly. It is good, and I will make it again, but I think I'll add some garlic powder, salt and pepper, and seasoned salt. 

This recipe is a great base on which to build a really tasty dish.
definitely tasty!!!
used boneless pork chops and added minced garlic in lemon pepper. Family loved it. I have been told to make this again
I made just as is except I put them wrapped in tin foil on a cookie sheet and glad I did. Would’ve burned my house down. One step that definitely should not have been omitted.
This was so good! I was able to cut the chops with a fork. My family voted it is a mske again
It tasted great. However my entire apartment filled up with smoke. Not sure I will do this again.
Had small boneless pork chops, used too much butter (if there's such a thing!) and oil. Otherwise delicious! and simple to make
Tried this with very good quality boneless pork chops; sadly, they came out rather tough. Not great.
